best_field_traits: Usually creeping or ascending warm-season annual, frequently in disturbed moist sites.
Racemes relatively slender with spaced tiny spikelets rather than dense plump cylindrical clusters.
Spikelets much smaller (~1.5–2.5 mm) than U. texana; lower glume almost minute, ~15–25% of length.
Upper glume and sterile lemma occupy most of spikelet; tough fertile lemma and palea transversely wrinkled.
Creeping basal shoots may root at nodes; must be seen/photographed to assert.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole plant with any actual stem node rooting
Panicle in profile showing loose branch spacing
Individual tiny mature spikelet with calibrated scale
Macro tiny clasping lower glume versus U. texana
True collar ligule and sheath hair bases
crew_field_check: FIRST PHOTO: count the radiating flowering racemes; observe tiny attached spikelets but do not claim individual glumes are visibly resolved.
COLLECT a ripe unit and MEASURE 1.5–2.2 mm spikelets with an actual 1-mm ruler; their PAIRED arrangement on a three-angled rachis may require close view.
Under 10–20× look for lower glume a small clasping, often truncate 1/8–1/4-length bract; a thumb-sized plant picture cannot show this.
Trace a living stem horizontally until a true basal NODE and roots emerge; root position has not been photographed in the stored image.
Exclude Digitaria using true spikelet arrangement and ligule/collar anatomy, not just fingerlike radiating head geometry.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Despite the photo's spread-out branches, published U. reptans descriptions report 5–15 often closely spaced racemes with crowded PAIRED spikelets along each branch; a 'loose head' alone is misleading. U. fusca has typically larger plumper ~2.4–3.4 mm spikelets, lower glume ~1/4–1/3, and U. texana much larger 4.5–5.9 mm units with lower glume reaching roughly half to two-thirds.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Measure 5–10 ripe spikelets and a detached lower glume from each plant; compare paired attachments under the same 1-mm scale.
field_matrix.separating_characters: Creeping U. reptans typically has 1.5–2.2 mm spikelets (some regional descriptions 2–2.5 mm), a truncate cufflike lower glume about 1/8–1/4 of spikelet length (UT ~0.5 mm), and crowded paired spikelets. U. fusca is larger, usually 2.4–3.4 mm, with a longer lower glume (UT ~1–1.3 mm) and conspicuous cross-veins on upper glume/lower lemma. Both are annual and may root at lower nodes.
field_matrix.caution: Small ranges overlap at their extremes and no existing unscaled overview photograph proves a glume ratio; hold Urochloa sp. if no ripe, vouchered dissection.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Put mature spikelets of both species beside one millimeter ruler; expose the lower glume and the actual blade–sheath junction.
field_matrix.separating_characters: U. reptans has tiny 1.5–2.2 mm spikelets and a ~0.2–0.6 mm truncate lower glume (about 1/8–1/4); U. texana has 4.5–5.9 mm spikelets and a ~2.4–3.2 mm lower glume (about 1/2–2/3). Reptans has a short hair-fringe ligule, whereas texana has a ~1–1.8 mm ciliate membrane. Both can have lower nodes that root, so habit alone is insufficient.
field_matrix.caution: Do not claim that distant head photographs prove a ligule or glume length. Photograph both ripe spikelets and true collars with scale before attaching anatomical arrows.

not_reliable_alone: Equating 'reptans' name with verified roots on the photographed plant
Teaching this species as necessarily a loose/sparse inflorescence: spikelets are often paired and crowded
Using a star-shaped head alone to separate Digitaria from Urochloa

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.look_here_first: CREEPING SIGNALGRASS: inspect an actual decumbent annual stem rooting at its lower nodes, then the short one-sided racemes with crowded PAIRS of small spikelets. Use a ruler on a ripe spikelet (Kew 1.5–2.2 mm; WFO regional treatment 2–2.5 mm), then inspect the very short cufflike LOWER GLUME, not just the radiating head.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.measured_growth_and_collar: Kew/GrassBase: annual culms 15–60 cm, often rooting at lower nodes; blades 2–8 cm × 3–15 mm. Ligule a FRINGE OF HAIRS, with World Flora Online regional treatment describing ciliate ligule about 1 mm. Photograph the true junction with blade and sheath both attached, not adjacent sheath-mouth hairs.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.measured_racemes_and_spikelets: Kew/GrassBase: 5–15 unilateral racemes, each 1–4 cm, on a central 1–8 cm axis, spikelets crowded in two rows and usually paired, ciliate pedicels, angular/three-sided rachis. WFO regional treatment reports 3–6(–12) racemes and 2–2.5 mm spikelets, illustrating regional variation. Count branches on one mature plant; use 1-mm scale to distinguish U. reptans from U. fusca and U. texana.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.measured_glumes_lemmas_awns: Kew/GrassBase/AusGrass: ripe spikelet about 1.5–2.2 mm (WFO up to 2.5). LOWER GLUME cufflike/orbicular, about 0.4–0.6 mm and 1/8–1/4 total spikelet length, hyaline, truncate, generally 0–1-veined. UPPER GLUME about 1.7–2.2 mm, ~spikelet-length, about 7-veined (WFO 5–9). Lower sterile/staminate floret has a membranous ~1.7–2.2 mm five-veined lemma and a palea. Upper fertile lemma is HARD, wrinkled, about 1–2 mm, margins rolled inward, apex minutely mucronate. No conspicuous long lemma awn: tiny mucro is not a long awn. The glumes, lower sterile lemma and upper fertile lemma are separate structures.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.local_lookalikes: Within the three canonical signalgrasses, U. reptans has the smallest ripe spikelets (Kew 1.5–2.2 mm), with the lower glume only 1/8–1/4 length; U. fusca typically 2.4–3.4 mm and ~1/4–1/3; U. texana 4.5–5.9 mm and ~1/2–2/3. Branch angle/number overlaps, so confirm ripe spikelet size and actual lower glume proportion. Creeping stems must be seen rooted at real nodes; don't label a bent culm as rooting.
precise_photo_arrow_holds: Source-verified entire living plant with mature head AND soil-level lower stem visibly rooting at 2+ nodes, centimeter scale; do not infer root attachment from detached stem.
One intact mature raceme with PAIRS of spikelets, ciliate pedicels and three-angled rachis, 1-mm ruler; arrows only to visible pair/pedicel/rachis.
Dissected 1.5–2.2 mm mature spikelet with scale and separate arrows for tiny 0.4–0.6 mm cufflike lower glume, ~1.7–2.2 mm upper glume and lower sterile lemma.
Dissected upper hard wrinkled 1–2 mm fertile lemma and involute palea, at 20–40×; show terminal mucro, NOT an invented long awn.
Same-plant true hair-fringed ligule/collar at 10–20× with 1-mm calibration; distinguish ligule hairs from sheath-edge cilia.
Matched measured mature spikelet series for U. reptans, U. fusca and U. texana with independent exact-taxon image rights.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.public_ready_criteria: Retain all existing original photos, their source and per-image license records, provisional review labels, and native-range/taxonomy holds. Do not claim new photo bytes, validated microscopic arrows or site publication. FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS until exact-taxon publicly reusable rooted/collar/dissection photos and pixel-checked annotations are available and the ordinary public learner has passed QA.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.evidence_scope: Measurements reflect source descriptions, not actual gallery pixels. Regional Kew versus WFO branch and spikelet ranges are labeled rather than silently merged. Preserve prior native/taxonomic review.

locally_archived_gallery_20261023.needs: Real measured ligule and collar; mature dissected spikelet photographed with glumes and lemma; validate local lookalikes and arrows

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Urochloa reptans: first photo then mature-spikelet confirmation
steps: FIRST TWO PUBLIC PHOTOS: the Dan Johnson CC BY 4.0 and 葉子 CC0 records are species-labelled living Urochloa reptans. Use them for general taxon context only; their true ligules, individual glumes and rooted nodes are not pixel-certified.

PUBLIC LESSON RIGHTS: noncommercial-only CC BY-NC photos including excellent original mature-spikelet images are held outside the public gallery pending an independently transferable permission or an unrestricted replacement. Do not claim they are public released.

Collect and measure a ripe 1.5–2.2 mm spikelet on a 1-mm ruler: paired units along angular rachis and the very small lower glume are important, but neither open-licensed image presently establishes these characters.
Open a source-verified same-plant blade–sheath junction, record the approximately 1-mm hair-fringed ligule at 10–20×, and distinguish the actual collar from adjacent sheath hairs.
Trace a living stem to a real soil-contact lower node with attached adventitious roots rather than assuming the decumbent habit from a seedhead shot.
Compare with real independently credited U. fusca and U. texana, and exclude Digitaria using mature spikelet arrangement and collar/ligule, not merely radiating flowering branches.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Rank photos by what they truly show: flowering branch/shape first, followed by mature spikelet length and lower glume measured under 10–20×. Do not treat unmeasured photogenic heads as proof of native versus introduced species.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Strict site display filter removes five CC BY-NC teaching panels (four same species, one U. fusca comparison). Six publicly eligible panels remain, of which only two represent U. reptans. No true ligule, glume dissection or rooted node photographed at diagnostic quality. Scientific photo gaps and Pages render QA remain.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — FOLLOW THE STEM
field_id_short_tiles.short: Creeping/ascending ANNUAL; look for actual roots at lower nodes.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Trace a living flowering stem to its fibrous-rooted base and check whether lower nodes really produce adventitious roots. Both currently public same-species photographs (panels 1–2) are general plant references, NOT proof of a connected rooted node. Do not draw a rooting-node arrow on either.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · TRACE THE FLOWERING RACEMES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Usually 5–15 one-sided racemes, about 1–4 cm long.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Published accounts describe 5–15 short one-sided racemes about 1–4 cm long, with crowded paired spikelets; some regional descriptions give 3–6(–12) racemes. The two publicly eligible U. reptans panels are general source-labelled plants, not verified measured branch/spikelet anatomy. The better archived CC BY-NC reproductive macros are retained for evidence but are NOT in the public gallery; do not reference their former panel positions.
field_id_short_tiles.status: FIELD HEAD CUE — NO PUBLIC MEASURED RACEME/SPIKELET PHOTO

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · TRUE COLLAR, NOT SHEATH HAIRS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Ligule is a short ~1 mm HAIR FRINGE.
field_id_short_tiles.details: The true ligule is a short hair fringe (regional treatment ~1 mm). Open the inner blade–sheath junction on the same plant and photograph it at 10–20× with a 1-mm scale. No current public U. reptans panel resolves this structure, so this tile intentionally has no photo reference or ligule arrow.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · MEASURE A RIPE SPIKELET
field_id_short_tiles.details: Measure 5–10 mature U. reptans spikelets beside a 1-mm ruler (Kew about 1.5–2.2 mm; regional treatments to ~2.5 mm). Separate the tiny truncate/cufflike lower glume (~0.4–0.6 mm, 1/8–1/4 total length), nearly spikelet-length upper glume (~1.7–2.2 mm; about 5–9 veins depending on treatment), and lower sterile lemma. The genuine archived reproductive macros are CC BY-NC and withheld from the public gallery; neither current open-license subject panel proves a measured glume.
field_id_short_tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — NO PUBLIC SCALED TARGET-SPECIES GLUME

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · FIND THE FLORETS AND AWN ORIGIN
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower sterile/male floret + upper HARD wrinkled fertile lemma.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Dissect a ripe spikelet to show the lower sterile/staminate floret (membranous five-veined lemma and palea) and the upper hard, transversely wrinkled fertile lemma (roughly 1–2 mm, inrolled margins). The tiny terminal mucro is NOT a long projecting awn. No current public U. reptans image proves these structures, so do not link a look-alike photo or place speculative arrows.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · COMPARE AND RELEASE GATE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Smaller spikelets than U. fusca and U. texana; not FINISHED.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Current public gallery panels 3–6 (zero-based indices 2–5) are ALL different-species comparisons: U. fusca reproductive and vegetative images and U. texana habit/panicle. Published ripe-spikelet ranges: U. reptans ~1.5–2.2 mm with lower glume ~1/8–1/4; U. fusca ~2.4–3.4 mm with lower glume often ~1/4–1/3; U. texana ~4.5–5.9 mm with lower glume ~1/2–2/3. No same-scale comparison is currently verified. NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: actual rooted nodes, measured true hair-fringe ligule, scaled ripe paired spikelets and dissected glumes/lemmas with public rights. NEEDS_SITE_QA: confirm all six current panels, four different-species labels, original arrow endpoints, rights filtering and mobile render. Remain FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS.

grass_species_finalization_20261027.scope: Reconcile six field-ID tile indices with the current rights-filtered six-panel gallery; do not imply archived CC BY-NC anatomy is publicly visible.
grass_species_finalization_20261027.look_here_first: Seek an actual lower stem node rooting in soil, then crowded paired spikelets on short unilateral racemes. Confirm a ripe 1.5–2.2 mm spikelet and minute lower glume under scale; a star-shaped head alone is insufficient.
grass_species_finalization_20261027.measurable_anatomy: Literature (not gallery measurements): short hair-fringe ligule (~1 mm in a regional treatment); spikelet 1.5–2.2 mm (some regional treatments 2–2.5); lower glume ~0.4–0.6 mm, 1/8–1/4 spikelet length, 0–1 vein; upper glume ~1.7–2.2 mm, generally 7 veins (regional 5–9); lower sterile lemma ~1.7–2.2 mm, 5 veins; upper fertile hard transversely wrinkled lemma ~1–2 mm with tiny terminal mucro, NO long awn. Distinguish glume, sterile lemma, fertile lemma and palea.
NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: Authenticated Texas flowering plant showing the SAME continuous basal runner and actual roots emerging at two lower nodes, with centimeter scale.
Same-vouchered true inner hair-fringe ligule at opened blade–sheath collar, 10–20× and 1-mm ruler; distinguish from sheath-mouth cilia.
